To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Nyquist approach to the prediction of the gain and stability characteristics of negative conductance amplifiers is particularly useful for microwave tunnel-diode reflection amplifiers, 2) the immitance of the tunnel diode, viewed either in series or in parallel, is a function of frequency, and 3) a procedure is outlined for the construction of immitance curves of tunnel-diode amplifiers.

The stability of microwave reflection amplifiers is determined by the Nyquist plot of the complex reflection coefficient of the amplifier viewed as a parallel network, which is equivalent to the Smith chart representation of the complex input reflection coefficient of the same amplifier viewed as a series network.
the use of a tunnel-diode in a reflection configuration as the active device in a microwave amplifier is an effective method of obtaining amplification.

the development of a new class of microwave amplifiers based on the negative conductance properties of the tunnel-diodes.
the design of a high power amplifier for use in a high power radar system.
the development of a new method for the design of microwave tunnel diode reflection amplifiers.

the Nyquist approach to amplifier stability is a valuable and powerful technique for the design of reflection amplifiers of all types.
the method described is a very useful one, and that the results are of considerable value.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Nyquist chart can be used for stability analysis of microwave reflection amplifiers and the tunnel-diode immitance can be represented on the chart by means of a simple procedure.
we have shown how the Nyquist approach to amplifier stability can be applied to a class of negative conductance devices which have not previously been treated in this manner.

the Nyquist approach to microwave amplifier stability analysis has been extended to include the case of negative conductance amplifiers, and that the technique is particularly useful in predicting the stability of negative conductors embedded in networks of complicated functions of frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Nyquist approach is a very useful tool for stability analysis of microwave reflection amplifiers, and that it has the advantage over the more traditional Nyquist approach of requiring predominantly graphical computations.
the stability and gain of tunnel-diode reflection amplifiers can be simultaneously predicted by a graphical technique.
the Nyquist approach can be used in the design of reflection amplifiers, and that the stability and gain of these amplifiers can be simultaneously predicted by a single chart.
